organizations.Organization: TUM MIRMI (Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence)
organizations.What they build: TUM integrative research institute for robotics, perception and AI with over 70 professors; human-centered robots for health, work, environment and mobility, plus a doctoral program, visitor program and entrepreneurship network.
organizations._relationship_reason: Largest robotics institute in the Munich hub; a student lab can realistically get talks, lab visits or a co-supervised student project, not funding.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public 'Network & Partner' and 'TUM MIRMI Visitor Program' pages; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: KIT lab building the ARMAR humanoid family, KIT gripper hands and exoskeletons, and open software such as ArmarX, Simox and the MMM human-motion database; research on grasping and learning from human observation.
organizations._relationship_reason: Open datasets (human motion, bimanual actions) and ArmarX/Simox code are directly usable by students; speaker or visit is the realistic ask.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact page on h2t.iar.kit.edu; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Robot-learning lab (Prof. Jan Peters) working on reinforcement and imitation learning on real robots: robot juggling, on-robot self-play learning, blind humanoid skateboarding, physics-informed deep models for locomotion and the torque-controlled humanoid HAINER.
organizations._relationship_reason: One of Europe's most cited robot-learning groups, exactly our wedge (learning on real hardware); a talk or paper-reading collaboration is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public team page; no personal introduction known.

organizations.Organization: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
organizations.What they build: German Aerospace Center institute building humanoids (Agile Justin, Rollin' Justin, neoDavid), arms, hands, legged and aerial robots for space and terrestrial assistance; spun off Agile Robots, Roboception, Sensodrive and others.
organizations._relationship_reason: Germany's flagship robotics hardware lab and spin-off factory; realistic: lab tour or speaker, plus role models for hardware startups.
organizations.Warm contact path: Innovation & Transfer pages on dlr.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Fraunhofer Institute for Material Flow and Logistics: develops the two-wheeled balancing transport robot evoBOT, robot swarms and embodied AI for intralogistics, and hosts a yearly conference on mobile robotics (140+ participants in 2026). Part of the Robotics Institute Germany.
organizations._relationship_reason: Applied logistics robotics with an open-source section; realistic ask is a speaker or visit, not hardware.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public contact via iml.fraunhofer.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.Organization: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
organizations.What they build: Basic research institute on intelligent systems that perceive, learn and act, combining theory, software and hardware (robotics, materials, optics, medical systems); co-founder of the Cyber Valley ecosystem.
organizations._relationship_reason: World-class ML and robotics researchers; a remote talk is the realistic ask.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known; public events page.

organizations.Organization: TU Dresden CeTI (Centre for Tactile Internet with Human-in-the-Loop)
organizations.What they build: Cluster of Excellence at TU Dresden on real-time human-robot interaction over networks (tactile internet, teleoperation, haptics); runs public robotics demos and a Mobile Robotics Hackathon (100+ participants in Oct 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Runs hackathons and teleoperation research, which fits a student lab joining an event; Dresden is the hub's main robotics research cluster.
organizations.Warm contact path: Events/news pages on ceti.one; no personal introduction known.

organizations.Organization: TU Berlin Robotics and Biology Laboratory (RBO)
organizations.What they build: TU Berlin lab (Prof. Oliver Brock) on robot manipulation, soft hands and interactive perception; the main university robotics group in Berlin.
organizations._relationship_reason: Berlin anchor for manipulation research; speaker or student exchange is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public contact robotics(at)robotics.tu-berlin.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.Organization: University of Bonn AIS (Autonomous Intelligent Systems)
organizations.What they build: Prof. Sven Behnke's group: NimbRo humanoid soccer robots (RoboCup AdultSize champions, e.g. RoboCup 2023 with NimbRo-OP2X and 3D-printed gears), service robots, bin picking, micro aerial vehicles and deep learning.
organizations._relationship_reason: Cologne/Bonn hub's leading robot lab with a strong student-competition culture; talk or RoboCup advice realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact on ais.uni-bonn.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.Organization: University of Hamburg TAMS (Technical Aspects of Multimodal Systems)
organizations.What they build: Group of Prof. Jianwei Zhang working on multimodal control, sensor-based manipulation, robot learning, human perception and HRI; hosts the Hamburg Bit-Bots RoboCup team's department.
organizations._relationship_reason: Hamburg hub's main robot-learning lab; speaker is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public contact on tams.informatik.uni-hamburg.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: German Research Center for AI unit with about 125 staff building mobile robots for space, underwater, logistics, production and search and rescue; works with the University of Bremen robotics group (home of B-Human).
organizations._relationship_reason: Large applied lab with many legged and space robots; speaker or visit realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public contact on robotik.dfki-bremen.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: New technical university whose founding chair Wolfram Burgard (ex-Freiburg, mobile robotics and probabilistic robotics) leads AI and Robotics; offers an M.Sc. 'AI & Robotics' and has human-centered and assistive robotics groups.
organizations._relationship_reason: Young university looking for visibility and student exchange; a talk by its robotics professors is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: National robotics network launched in 2024 with BMBF backing and TUM as lead organisation (KIT, DLR, Fraunhofer and others as partners); shares software, data, labs and benchmarks, runs an innovation programme and a lecture series by leading robotics researchers.
organizations._relationship_reason: Its public lecture series, shared benchmarks and challenges are an easy way to plug a foreign student lab into German robotics.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public RIG HQ team page; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Europe's AI research and startup ecosystem around MPI-IS and the universities of Stuttgart and Tübingen, with research groups, a start-up network, an AI incubator and investor/corporate networks.
organizations._relationship_reason: Start-up network and incubator events are the realistic entry; not a sponsor for foreign students.
organizations.Warm contact path: Cyber Valley start-up network pages; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: TUM-born project for musculoskeletal (muscle and tendon) humanoid robots that grew into a 50+ student team and a not-for-profit research company; competed in the ANA Avatar XPRIZE and has now become 'Robodies'.
organizations._relationship_reason: The best German example of a student-run robot lab becoming a research company; ideal peers and speakers.
organizations.Warm contact path: Student Teams/Contact page on roboy.org; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Student and researcher RoboCup team of the University of Bremen and DFKI; 13-time world champion in the RoboCup Humanoid (formerly Standard Platform) Soccer League with NAO robots, with open-source code releases and datasets.
organizations._relationship_reason: Open-source code and team reports are a ready-made curriculum for multi-robot software; peer exchange realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Team/Supporters pages on b-human.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: RoboCup student club of the University of Hamburg; built the open Wolfgang-OP humanoid and took 2nd place in the Humanoid League small-size division at RoboCup 2026 (Incheon).
organizations._relationship_reason: Open ROS 2 humanoid software and hardware; a peer club we could copy or meet at RoboCup German Open.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact/Mitmachen pages on bit-bots.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: AI student initiative at TUM (150+ students from 30+ universities) running research projects, industry projects, a startup incubator (ELAB) and hackathons including the 500+ participant TUM.ai Makeathon.
organizations._relationship_reason: Closest German peer to 42AI (student AI association); co-hosting events or inviting each other's teams is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Partner/Become a Member pages on tum-ai.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Berlin hacker space styled as a 'space station under Berlin' (c-base e.V.); hacker house / makerspace with regular meetups (NixOS, net policy) and events.
organizations._relationship_reason: Low-cost venue/community in Berlin for a meetup or demo night; no robotics funding.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public events calendar on c-base.org; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Makerspace (fab lab) run by RWTH Aachen's Media Computing Group, open for digital fabrication (laser cutting, 3D printing) and research projects.
organizations._relationship_reason: Aachen makerspace for fabrication-heavy prototypes; only useful if we travel there.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public flyer and contact on fablab.rwth-aachen.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Makerspace for hardtech and deep tech founded in 2018: workshops, a Hardtech Innovation Accelerator and events; 110+ startups have been based there; opening ringberlin (17,000 m2) in 2027.
organizations._relationship_reason: Hardware makerspace and accelerator; realistic: event space or accelerator contact for a hardware startup spun out of the lab.
organizations.Warm contact path: Programs/Events pages on motionlab.berlin; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Makerspace of UnternehmerTUM (Europe's large innovation and founder centre at TUM) with CNC mills, 3D printers and workshops, plus corporate innovation sprints (e.g. a SICK 5-day sprint in Nov 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Paid machine access and innovation sprints with corporates; the realistic way to prototype in Munich or join a sprint.
organizations.Warm contact path: Course booking on maker-space.de; UnternehmerTUM contact form. No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Jungheinrich company (160+ experts) building intelligent mobile robots for intralogistics: the picking robot TORU and the autonomous tugger/KLT robot SOTO.
organizations._relationship_reason: Pioneer of perception-driven picking robots in Munich; speaker on deploying mobile manipulators is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact page on magazino.eu; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Hamburg material-handling group (forklifts, warehouse automation) that owns Magazino; its mobile robot EAE 212a won an iF Design Award 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Large buyer of warehouse robotics; sponsorship is possible but would go through Magazino or HR/innovation teams.
organizations.Warm contact path: Corporate contact on jungheinrich.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Bosch's AI research centre; in 2026 with Carnegie Mellon it published Humanoid Transformer with Touch Dreaming (HTD) for tactile humanoid loco-manipulation using RL and VR data collection.
organizations._relationship_reason: Publishes robot-learning research close to our wedge; speaker or research contact realistic, sponsorship less so.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Ground-autonomy platform with human-assisted (teleoperated) autonomy for yard trucks, container terminals and defence logistics; Gen 4 vehicle kit; Series A extended with €18M in 2025 to €75M total funding.
organizations._relationship_reason: Teleoperation-plus-autonomy is a clear real-world case study; speaker is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact page on fernride.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Defence-tech startup building the modular Gereon unmanned ground vehicle, the Mithra OS software layer and the Hector system for European armed forces.
organizations._relationship_reason: Defence focus limits fit with a student lab; only a talk on rugged field robotics is realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact page on arx-robotics.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Automation company founded in 2019: online robot marketplace and configurator plus the turnkey MalocherBot automation cell for SMEs.
organizations._relationship_reason: Good example of selling robotics to SMEs; speaker possible.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact info@unchainedrobotics.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: DLR spin-off making 3D stereo vision sensors (rc_visard NG, rc_visard, rc_viscore) and the rc_reason software suite for bin picking, CAD matching and SLAM.
organizations._relationship_reason: 3D vision sensor maker that could loan a sensor or give a perception talk.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact info@roboception.de (Munich); no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Construction-robotics startup building modular, AI-enabled robots that work directly on existing structures (e.g. concrete renovation); raised €4M pre-seed in Feb 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Very early startup open to student contacts; real unstructured-environment problem.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Autonomy operating system for agricultural machinery makers (navigation with or without GNSS for open fields, orchards and horticulture, mission control, coverage planner); runs Autonomy Days in Osnabrück and a farming meetup at Gate Garching (Nov 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Runs its own public events (incl. Munich-area meetup); speaker or event visit realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Events page on naturerobots.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Hamburg startup building robotic kitchen systems that cook fresh meals autonomously ('physical AI for autonomous food infrastructure'), combining AI robots with digital kitchen operations.
organizations._relationship_reason: Consumer-facing robotics with a filmable product; speaker realistic.
organizations.Warm contact path: Contact form on goodbytz.com; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Spin-off of West Coast University of Applied Sciences building an AI laser-weeding robot that recognises weeds and burns them; serial production started with sales from 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Small agri-robotics team using vision-based weeding, a good perception case study.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Defence AI company building the Clarity agentic intelligence platform, the HX-2 precision-strike drone, the CA-1 Europa uncrewed combat aircraft and maritime autonomy systems.
organizations._relationship_reason: Major Munich autonomy employer but defence weapons; at most a technical talk, and the lab may decide to avoid it.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Munich early-stage and growth VC linked to UnternehmerTUM investing in B2B deeptech, climatetech, mobility and software/AI; closed its fourth fund at €250M (AUM over €600M), with initial tickets up to €10M.
organizations._relationship_reason: Deep-tech investor in the TUM ecosystem; realistic: pitch feedback for a lab spin-off.
organizations.Warm contact path: No personal introduction known; via UnternehmerTUM programs.

organizations.What they build: Germany's most active public-private seed VC, investing from pre-seed to growth (up to €30M per company in growth rounds) in companies no older than three years.
organizations._relationship_reason: Typical first institutional cheque for German robotics spin-offs; realistic: office hours or pitch feedback.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public application route on htgf.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: German federal agency financing breakthrough innovations through challenges (e.g. AI-native chip design, circular biomanufacturing) and funded projects.
organizations._relationship_reason: Runs open challenges teams can enter; no current robotics challenge seen, so medium fit.
organizations.Warm contact path: Open calls on sprind.org; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Annual hacker conference of the Chaos Computer Club between Christmas and New Year in Hamburg (40C3: 27-30 Dec 2026), with talks, hardware hacking and a 'Junghacker:innentag' for young makers (soldering, 3D printing).
organizations._relationship_reason: Huge maker/hacker audience where a robot demo or talk gives visibility at near-zero cost.
organizations.Warm contact path: Call for participation on events.ccc.de; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: TUM.ai's yearly Makeathon (500+ participants) with industry challenges; part of TUM.ai's hackathon and talk series.
organizations._relationship_reason: Large student AI hackathon where a robotics team could compete; travel from Paris required.
organizations.Warm contact path: Via TUM.ai events page; no personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: Two-day mobile robotics hackathon run by TU Dresden's CeTI cluster; 100+ participants in October 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Rare robotics-specific student hackathon in Germany; good target for a team trip.
organizations.Warm contact path: Events/news on ceti.one; no personal introduction known.

robots_models.Name: ARMAR humanoid family
robots_models.Key specs: Series of KIT humanoids with KIT hands, used for grasping, bimanual manipulation and learning from human observation; individual specs unknown here.
robots_models.Why it matters: Germany's best-known academic humanoid line; shows a full research humanoid stack (ArmarX) end to end.

robots_models.Name: ArmarX
robots_models.Key specs: Robot software framework and control architecture used on the ARMAR humanoids, alongside the Simox simulation/planning toolbox.
robots_models.Why it matters: Open framework students can study to see how a humanoid's software is organised.

robots_models.Name: Agile Justin
Built by: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
robots_models.Key specs: Humanoid upper body on a mobile base used as a platform for learning-based dexterous manipulation.
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference platform for AI dexterous manipulation in Europe.

robots_models.Name: Rollin' Justin
Built by: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
robots_models.Key specs: Wheeled humanoid for household and space-assistance research (teleoperation from orbit studies).
robots_models.Why it matters: Classic example of a wheeled humanoid for assistance tasks.

robots_models.Name: neoDavid
Built by: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
robots_models.Key specs: Robust humanoid with variable-stiffness actuation and skilful manipulation.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows how compliant actuators make humanoids robust to impacts.

robots_models.Name: HAINER
robots_models.Key specs: Torque-controlled humanoid used for learning-based control research.
robots_models.Why it matters: Torque control plus robot learning, the kind of research our lab wants to follow.

robots_models.Name: evoBOT
robots_models.Key specs: Two-wheeled, dynamically balancing (inverted pendulum) modular transport robot for load carriers and human-robot collaboration; fewer actuators than a humanoid.
robots_models.Why it matters: Cheap-to-build alternative to humanoids for logistics; balancing control is a nice student topic.

robots_models.Name: TORU
robots_models.Key specs: Autonomous mobile picking robot that picks small boxes (originally shoe boxes) from shelves; now also spare parts and e-commerce items.
robots_models.Why it matters: One of the first perception-driven mobile picking robots in production.

robots_models.Name: SOTO
robots_models.Key specs: Autonomous KLT (small load carrier) robot / tugger for line feeding in production.

robots_models.Name: rc_visard NG
robots_models.Key specs: 3D stereo sensor with on-board edge processing running the rc_reason software (bin picking, CAD matching, SLAM).
robots_models.Why it matters: Industrial 3D vision sensor for grasping projects.

robots_models.Name: Wolfgang-OP
robots_models.Key specs: Kid-size soccer humanoid of the Hamburg Bit-Bots with public software repository.
robots_models.Why it matters: Open student-built humanoid; shows what a student team can build.

robots_models.Name: NimbRo-OP2X
Built by: University of Bonn AIS (Autonomous Intelligent Systems)
robots_models.Key specs: Adult-size soccer humanoid with 3D-printed gears and new-generation actuators; won RoboCup 2023 AdultSize (66:0 goals).
robots_models.Why it matters: Proof that 3D-printed humanoids can win world championships.

robots_models.Name: Roboy 3.0
robots_models.Key specs: Musculoskeletal humanoid using muscles and tendons, developed for the ANA Avatar XPRIZE era.
robots_models.Why it matters: Student-built bio-inspired humanoid; strong outreach story.

robots_models.Name: MalocherBot
robots_models.Key specs: Modular turnkey automation cell for SMEs, configured through Unchained's online configurator.
robots_models.Why it matters: Example of packaging cobots for small manufacturers.

robots_models.Name: FERNRIDE Gen 4 vehicle kit
robots_models.Key specs: Fourth-generation autonomy/teleoperation retrofit kit for yard and terminal trucks, aimed at series production (2024).
robots_models.Why it matters: Human-assisted autonomy for heavy vehicles in real deployment.

robots_models.Name: Mithra OS
robots_models.Key specs: Software layer of ARX Robotics' unmanned ground systems (alongside Gereon UGV and Hector).
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows the robot-OS layer strategy of a German field-robotics startup.

robots_models.Name: Naiture laser weeding robot
robots_models.Key specs: Tractor-assisted robot that classifies crops vs weeds with AI and burns weeds by laser at 2-5 km/h; near 100% recognition claimed.

robots_models.Name: Humanoid Transformer with Touch Dreaming (HTD)
robots_models.Key specs: Policy for humanoid loco-manipulation that predicts touch and force outcomes; trained with RL and VR teleoperation data, fusing tactile, multi-view vision and proprioception.
robots_models.Why it matters: Recent German industrial lab result on tactile robot learning.

robots_models.Name: Nature Robots Farming Autonomy OS
robots_models.Key specs: Autonomy OS with hybrid localization (with or without GNSS/RTK), field coverage planner and browser mission control.
robots_models.Why it matters: Agri autonomy software sold to OEMs.

summary: Leaders: Munich dominates (TUM MIRMI, DLR RM, RIG HQ, UnternehmerTUM, plus NEURA/Agile/Franka/RobCo already mapped); Karlsruhe (KIT H2T), Darmstadt (IAS), Bonn (AIS), Bremen (DFKI, B-Human) and Dresden (CeTI) are the other academic poles.

Money: 2026 German robotics funding is concentrated in a few humanoid/industrial scale-ups already in Notion; newly mapped startups here are mostly seed/Series A (Sitegeist, Nature Robots, Naiture, goodBytz, Unchained) or defence (ARX, Helsing), with HTGF, UVC Partners and SPRIND as early public/deep-tech capital.
Demand: logistics (Jungheinrich/Magazino, Fraunhofer IML, FERNRIDE), construction and agriculture are the concrete buyers; defence autonomy is growing but a poor fit for a student lab.
Peers: TUM.ai, Roboy, B-Human and Hamburg Bit-Bots are the closest student counterparts to 42AI; Roboy shows the path from student team to research company.
Best entry point: pitch a joint LeRobot/robot-learning session to TUM.ai and TU Darmstadt IAS, and send a team to the CeTI Mobile Robotics Hackathon or the 40C3 Congress for low-cost visibility.
